number_of_offences: Six persons charged, four individuals and two entities finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation/planning as the appellant created the infrastructure for the fraudulent GDR issue
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the prosecution complaint filed by the Enforcement Directorate under Sections 44 and 45 of PMLA, which detailed the appellant's role in the fraudulent GDR issue and money-laundering activities.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the prosecution complaint and the role attributed to the appellant as detailed in the complaint, finding it sufficient to satisfy the conditions of Section 45 of PMLA.
post_offence_conduct: The appellant was in jail from 26.09.2022 and was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate on that date.
bail_history: Appellant directed to be enlarged on bail
trial_duration: FIR registered on 29.10.2013; trial judgment dated 07.12.2022; Supreme Court decision dated APRIL 20, 2023
legal_representation: R. Basant, Sr. Adv., M/s. Shakil Ahmad Syed, Tanmaya Mehta, Syed Ahmed Saud, Lalit Valecha, Daanish Ahmed Syed, Mohd Parvez Dabas, Uzmi Jameel Husain, Aqib Baig, Advs. for the Appellant; S. V. Raju, ASG, Mukesh Kumar Maroria, Zoheb Hussain, Annam Venkatesh, Ashok Panigrahi, Ms. Sairica Raju, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: ECIR lodged on 05.05.2022; prosecution complaint filed under Sections 44 and 45 of PMLA; no final report filed in FIR for the predicate offence for nine years
appeal_history: Trial court: No mention of judgment; High Court: Judgment dated 07.12.2022; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed on APRIL 20, 2023
prosecution_argument: The Enforcement Directorate filed a prosecution complaint under Sections 44 and 45 of PMLA, alleging that the appellant was the kingpin and mastermind behind fraudulent GDR transactions, and that he was directly involved in the process and activity connected with the proceeds of crime, including its acquisition.
defence_argument: The appellant's counsel argued that the appellant has been in jail without a charge-sheet being filed against him for over nine years, that he is a Chartered Accountant offering professional services within the framework of law, and that there is nothing in the prosecution complaint to show that he is in possession of 'the proceeds of crime'.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the twin conditions prescribed in Section 45 of PMLA, particularly the second condition in Clause (ii) of sub-section (1), to determine the justification for the appellant's continued incarceration.
other_sentence_order: The appellant was directed to be enlarged on bail in ECIR No.HYZO/26/2022, subject to conditions including surrendering his passport and regular appearances before the Special Court.
